sentences: Running a tournament shouldn't be harder than winning one.
Yet most organizers still juggle spreadsheets and group chats: drawing brackets by hand, chasing entry fees, and arguing about match times.
And players often wait weeks for their prize money.
Meet TurniRUM: an open-source tournament platform where AI does the organizing, and PayPal handles the money.
You run the event.
The bracket, the schedule and the prizes take care of themselves.
Here's how it works.
The web app runs on Supabase: a Postgres database protected by row-level security, and an Edge Function with all the business logic.
It asks Google Gemini to plan, uses PayPal for payments and payouts, and Brevo for email, while a scheduled job sends the reminders.
Let's see it in action.
An organizer simply describes the event: a Valorant cup for sixteen teams, twenty dollars entry, prizes for the top three.
Gemini fills in the whole form, from the rules and the schedule to the prize split and the bracket format.
The organizer confirms the ten percent platform fee, and publishes.
Players register their team and pay the entry fee with PayPal, using an account or a card.
Here we're in the PayPal sandbox, with a test card.
The server creates the order with the price from the database, captures it, and admits the team only after PayPal confirms the payment.
Card details never touch our servers.
When registration closes, one click lets the AI choose the format, seed the teams by their past results, and plan the schedule.
The bracket is ready, and every captain is notified.
Can't make your match?
When both captains press Reschedule, the AI moves it to a free slot with no clashes.
And reminders go out by email, a day and an hour before.
Need teammates?
The AI studies the tournaments you've played, and suggests players who fit, explaining every pick.
Results update the bracket and the standings live.
When the organizer finishes the tournament, TurniRUM settles the money automatically.
Prizes go straight to the winners' PayPal accounts through PayPal Payouts, ten percent goes to the platform, and the organizer withdraws the rest.
So Gemini works in seven places: drafting, formats, seeding, scheduling, rescheduling, reminders and teammate matching.
And there's always a safe fallback when a model is busy.
Organizers save hours and get paid fairly.
Players get clear brackets, fair schedules, and prizes paid automatically.
And clubs and communities can finally run paid events with full transparency.
TurniRUM.
Tournaments that run themselves.
Open source, on GitHub.
